turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'll go, ma'am, but I hope it's all right with you if I don't call her loudly, I don't want to disturb anyone in the house.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'll go, ma'am, right away.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm going, ma'am, I'll go and get Estella for you, right away.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella, child, come to me at once. I have no time for your young friend's excuses.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Come, Estella, do not dawdle. I am not a woman to be kept waiting.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: What is the meaning of this hesitation, child? Speak quickly and tell me what is amiss.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will play with me, child. I insist upon it.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I will not be disappointed, child. Estella, you see to this young boy's entertainment. I have no patience for frivolous excuses.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella, I have a proposition for you. Take this boy to the garden and play a game of croquet with him. I want to see him laugh, and I want to see you bring joy to him.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I don't know if I can, Miss Havisham. My sister, Sarah, is ill and needs me to care for her. I fear that if I leave her side, she may not recover.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I don't think I can play with you, Miss Havisham, not with my sister so poorly. I wouldn't want to be away from her even for a little while.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I was wondering, Miss Havisham, if there's anything I could do here to help your... um, lady, Estella, instead of going to the garden? I wouldn't want to be a bother, but perhaps I could assist her with something?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I wouldn't want to intrude, Miss Havisham, if there's nothing that needs doing, perhaps Estella could tell me what she needs my help with?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Thank you for considering my situation, Miss Havisham, but I fear I really must decline your invitation to play. I wouldn't want to disappoint you, but I must be with my sister.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I'm not very good company for a game, Miss Havisham, and I wouldn't want to be a burden, but perhaps I could help you with something in the house instead?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm not sure I'd be very good at helping you with anything, Miss Havisham, but I could try to be of some small use, if you think it would be of any help to you.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I don't mean to be impertinent, Miss Havisham, but I'm not sure I'd be very comfortable playing games with you, especially with Estella... she seems so... remote.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm not trying to be rude, Miss Havisham, but your house is so... grand, and I'm afraid I wouldn't know how to play the games you're used to.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm not sure what's proper, but I've never seen a house like this before, and I'm a bit overwhelmed, Miss Havisham.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I'd be in the way, Miss Havisham, and your house is so... so beautifully kept, I wouldn't want to risk making a mess or damaging anything.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.
